title: Rhapsody on Japanese Folk Songs
identity: Ryota Ishikawa's Rhapsody on Japanese Folk Songs is an original 2010 alto saxophone and piano work, published by Zen-On in 2014, commissioned by Nobuya Sugawa.

evidence.claim: Publisher confirms Alto Saxophone and Piano edition, SEO-025, product 560025, 32-page full score plus 12-page part, released 2014-05-15, about 13 minutes, commissioned by Nobuya Sugawa and premiered in 2010 by Sugawa and pianist Minako Koyanagi.
EAMDC describes the original version's commission, premiere, folk materials, and distinct orchestral version.
CiNii records printed score and part, alto saxophone and piano, Zen-On 2014, 31+12 pages.

Official Zen-On six-page public trial preview was opened. On the first notation page (printed p.4), the alto saxophone begins with long held tones before slurred moving figures; the piano introduces strongly accented, repeated chordal figures with low-register writing. The preview reveals the opening only, so no full-range or later-section claims are made.
evidence.source_name: Zen-On official public score trial, product 560025

score_observations: On the visually inspected opening score page (printed p.4), the alto saxophone starts with a long held tone, then proceeds into slurred moving figures; the piano uses strongly accented chordal attacks and low-register writing. A brief subsequent saxophone passage moves more actively over repeated piano sonorities. No complete range claim is made, and later sections were not present in the inspected sample.
review_focus: Inference: the documented quotation/evocation of multiple Japanese folk idioms and imitation of shamisen and shakuhachi provide contrasting style and timbre questions; exact saxophone technique awaits score inspection.

listening.description: The page links a performance of the alto saxophone and piano version.
listening.verification: Performer credits on publisher page; playback not audited.

score_links.description: Six-page publisher sample viewer; opening score page visually inspected.

gaps: The public preview included only the opening score page; later movements/material and full saxophone range were not inspected.
